title: Facilities, Buildings & Grounds Stewardship for Inspection Station Networks
capability_statement: Parsons operates large, geographically dispersed networks of vehicle inspection facilities and is positioned to take operational responsibility for the buildings, grounds, and on-site equipment supporting those facilities. Across our state inspection programs (PennDOT, Vermont DMV, Hawaii DOT, Texas DPS, Ontario MOECC, and the existing Northeast hybrid I/M program) we already coordinate station-level facility access, security sign-in/sign-out, and on-site equipment deployment, software certification, and ATP-driven equipment testing across thousands of inspection lanes. Our regional office structure (currently three I/M regional offices plus a centralized headquarters) demonstrates the dispatch-and-coverage model needed to deliver routine janitorial, grounds keeping, snow removal, HVAC, electrical, plumbing, alarm, and structural maintenance on a multi-site portfolio where some sites are wholly contractor-occupied and others are shared with the State. We bring a documented quality-assurance framework, a financial-stability profile (annual revenue exceeding $4.5 billion) sufficient to fund routine service and maintenance at our own expense and to carry monthly utility, alarm, and rental obligations, and a procurement and SCM-style approval workflow used today for capital decisions, escrow controls, third-party quotes, and proof-of-purchase documentation. Our facility assessment, capital planning, and OEM-aligned preventive-maintenance discipline already used for inspection equipment translates directly to building systems planning, the annual master inventory list, and the standardized PM/structural/property repair plan required within 180 days of contract effective date. For shared co-located areas we will operate to the SCM-approved scope at no additional charge, hold three independent quotes for remediation work, secure written approval before alterations, and conduct single-lane maintenance outside posted hours so that motorist-facing operations are not interrupted.

named_past_performance.name: Pennsylvania Vehicle Emissions I/M Program (PennDOT, 1997 to present)
named_past_performance.scope: Program management of one of the largest decentralized I/M programs in the United States, including station and equipment management across approximately 8,200 inspection stations in 25 counties; on-site equipment deployment, calibration, ATP, software certification, audits, sticker custody and reconciliation, and station compliance with Title 67 PA Code Chapter 175; regional office network in Pittsburgh, Harrisburg, and Philadelphia providing dispatchable coverage for site visits.
named_past_performance.outcome: Continuous program operation since 1997 supporting nearly 7 million inspections projected by 2025; over 306,000 covert audits and 228,000 safety audits conducted; demonstrated multi-site field operations that mirror the dispatch model needed for routine facility maintenance, grounds, and janitorial coverage.

named_past_performance.name: New Jersey Motor Vehicle Inspection System (MVC, 1998 to 2024)
named_past_performance.scope: Project and operations management of the Enhanced I/M Program including VIID development, equipment ATP, software certification, motorist call center, and on-site station management at 12 centralized inspection stations.
named_past_performance.outcome: 12 stations achieved OSHA Voluntary Protection Program (VPP) status under Parsons' operations, demonstrating sustained workplace safety, housekeeping, and facility-condition discipline at occupied operating sites.

named_past_performance.name: Vermont Automated Vehicle Inspection Program (Vermont DMV, 2016 to present)
named_past_performance.scope: Program management including a 6-month, 1,200-facility implementation requiring on-site equipment deployment, station coordination, and access procedures across the entire facility portfolio.
named_past_performance.outcome: Successful 6-month implementation across 1,200 facilities with sticker printing-on-demand, evidencing the multi-site mobilization tempo that supports a contractor-of-record taking over facilities, buildings, and grounds responsibility.

named_past_performance.name: Texas Automated Vehicle Inspection (Texas DPS, 2006 to present)
named_past_performance.scope: Program and software management including equipment software updates and field service across 6,700 private inspection stations in a decentralized program, with a service call ticketing and response tracking system.
named_past_performance.outcome: Equipment software updates pushed to 6,700 stations within four months of award, with a comprehensive service call ticketing and response tracking system integrated for ongoing field-service dispatch.

named_past_performance.name: Ontario Integrated Vehicle Safety and Emissions Inspection Program / DriveON (Ontario MOECC, 1999 to 2028)
named_past_performance.scope: Program and operations management of the LDV emissions program including facility certification, inspector training, fee collection, and migration of program systems to AWS without service interruption to existing emissions stations.
named_past_performance.outcome: Successful transition of the Ontario Heavy-Duty Emissions program to AWS cloud with no service interruption or facility impact to the existing emissions stations; 100% uptime on DriveON since April 2022.

named_past_performance.name: Hawaii Electronic Periodic Motor Vehicle Inspection Program (Hawaii DOT, 2013 to present)
named_past_performance.scope: Program and operations management, station billing, tablet-based software development, and statewide implementation including station outreach across the Hawaii station network.
named_past_performance.outcome: Met a four-month implementation timeline and rolled out sticker printing-on-demand across the program; demonstrated short-cycle multi-site mobilization across geographically distributed facilities.

differentiators: (1) Operating tenure across six concurrent state/provincial inspection programs gives Parsons direct, in-place experience with the access-controlled, sign-in/sign-out, security-protocol environment the RFP requires before any contractor personnel may enter a facility. (2) Demonstrated multi-site mobilization tempo (1,200 VT facilities in 6 months; 6,700 TX stations in 4 months) shows we can stand up the maintenance, janitorial, grounds, and snow-removal coverage matrix on day one of contract performance. (3) Existing OEM-aligned preventive maintenance discipline for inspection equipment, including ATP scripting, calibration, equipment testing and approval, and bill-of-sale/proof-of-ownership controls, directly supports the parallel PM, spare-parts, and equipment-purchase documentation requirements for facility equipment. (4) Three-region operational redundancy (Pittsburgh, Harrisburg, Philadelphia) plus remote-work proven during COVID-19 evidences the dispatch model and continuity needed for snow events, alarm calls, and after-hours single-lane maintenance windows. (5) NJ MVC OSHA VPP recognition at 12 Parsons-operated inspection stations provides third-party validation of housekeeping, hazard-control, and facility-condition standards. (6) Established procurement, escrow, and quote-comparison workflows already used on capital decisions translate directly to the three-quote remediation rule, written-approval-before-alteration rule, and SCM-approval workflow for capital repairs and Plan updates. (7) Publicly traded firm with $4.5B+ revenue and Employee Stock Ownership Trust governance has the balance-sheet depth to carry routine maintenance, alarm fees, utilities, and trailer-rental obligations at Contractor expense without cost recovery.
gap_notes: The Parsons evidence base for this theme establishes program-management and station-network experience but does NOT directly substantiate hands-on facilities, buildings, and grounds trade work. Capture team must source and attach: (a) for janitorial scope (A-002 carpet steam extraction twice yearly, A-012 HEPA-filter vacuuming, R-101 daily carpet vacuuming) - named janitorial subcontractor or self-perform plan with crew sizing, equipment lists, and HEPA equipment specifications; (b) for grounds keeping (A-028 monthly rough-lawn mowing of drainage ditches, catch basins, wood lots, transitions) - landscaping subcontractor or self-perform plan including equipment, frequencies, and drainage-area access procedures; (c) for snow removal - no Parsons evidence in the provided chunks addresses snow-removal capability, equipment, or response-time SLAs; this is a complete gap; (d) for HVAC maintenance per PEOSH (A-086) - no Parsons evidence describes mechanical-trades capability for HVAC, electrical, plumbing, water/waste systems on contractor-operated buildings; the company's facility experience in evidence is limited to inspection-equipment maintenance rather than building-systems trades, so a teaming partner or named HVAC subcontractor with PEOSH-compliant track record must be identified; (e) for the standardized PM/structural-repair/property-repair Plan (A-072, due within 180 days of contract effective date) - no template Plan from a prior project is in evidence; (f) for the annual master inventory list (A-034) - no example deliverable is in evidence and the format/scope must be developed; (g) for energy-efficient lighting/appliance replacement (A-053, EO 54 / N.J.S.A. 52:34-6.4) - no statute-specific compliance approach is in evidence and a New Jersey-jurisdiction reference will be needed; (h) for the Randolph Service Core trailer (M-030, ~$300/month) - the Parsons evidence does not address trailer leasing or hookup-cost handling and the capture team must confirm whether the existing trailer will be assumed, replaced, or relocated; (i) for shared co-located area repairs at no additional charge (A-095, R-002) - while Parsons has the financial capacity to absorb such costs, no past-performance example of repeated no-charge shared-area work is in evidence and a teaming case study should be sought; (j) for the historical Appendix 3.2G capital-expenditure baseline (R-004, M-048) - the capture team must obtain Appendix 3.2G itself and incorporate the historical FY2009 to FY2024 spend ranges into pricing assumptions; (k) for facility regulations/security protocol observance (R-047, R-056) - while Parsons' on-site operations show repeated state-facility access experience, the specific NJ MVC sign-in/sign-out and security-protocol procedures must be captured and documented; (l) for site-specific lighting-level adequacy testing (A-091) - no methodology in evidence; (m) most named past performance evidence references retired-state names (Pennsylvania, New Jersey MVC, Vermont, Hawaii, Ontario, Texas DPS) - in the Parsons Solution Catalog these descriptions can stand, but any narrative re-used in a New Jersey-specific proposal must keep these as separate prior projects rather than blending them into the current solicitation's voice; (n) ScreenForms/installation evidence references R-001 and R-004 hex-bolt and roller-assembly torque procedures from an installation manual, indicating Parsons-installed equipment has documented installation procedures, but this is at the work-instruction level and must be supplemented with a project-level equipment-installation past-performance narrative.
